notes.text: The Hebrew kibrat, a stretch of ground of unknown length, carried into Greek untranslated; the printed page has it in lower case, where the digital module capitalises it, and the transcription follows the page.
δυστοκέω, one sense, *to be in sore travail*, said of women.

reading: [[having lifted off|having lifted off, having carried off, having taken away, having removed from, having led away, having sailed and marched away and departed]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] [[name:Βαιθηλ]] [[made fast|made fast, fixed in the earth and planted, fastened together and constructed and built, made solid and stiff and hard, froze, became solid and stiff, became congealed and froze]] the [[the covered place|the covered place, the tent, the camp, the dwelling-place, the temple]] of him [[on yonder side|on yonder side, beyond, the part beyond and the far side]] [[of the tower|of the tower, of the city wall, of the moving tower]] [[name:Γαδερ]]. [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[at which time|at which time, when, since, whenever]] [[brought near|brought near, brought up to, approached, was imminent, approximated to, was next of kin, was on the point of]] [[name:χαβραθα]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[earth|earth, land, the ground]] [[to come|to come, to go, to go back and return, to be going to and intend, to come within a little of and be near]] of [[name:Εφραθα]], [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced]] [[name:Ραχηλ]] and [[was in sore travail|was in sore travail]] [[in birth|within, inside of, and by means of birth, delivery]].

names.gloss: (Γαδερ, from Hebrew ʿĒder, "flock")
(χαβραθα, the Hebrew kibrat left untranslated, a stretch of ground of unknown length)
(Εφραθα, from Hebrew ʾEprātâ, usually connected with pārâ, "to be fruitful")
(Ραχηλ, from Hebrew Rāḥēl, "ewe")

greek: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ σκληρῶς αὐτὴν τίκτειν εἶπεν αὐτῇ ἡ μαῖα Θάρσει, καὶ γὰρ οὗτός σοί ἐστιν υἱός.
hint: And it happened, as she was giving birth hard, the midwife said to her: Take courage, for this also is a son for you.

notes.text: μαῖα, *good mother, dame* first, and *a midwife* last: the word is a form of address before it is a trade.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus omits σοί.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[in|within, inside of, and by means of]] the [[hard|hard, harsh and crashing, stiff and unyielding, stiff and sturdy, austere and severe]] her [[to bring into the world|to bring into the world, to bring forth, to bear, to produce]] [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] to her the [[the good mother|the good mother, the dame, the fostermother and nurse, the true mother, the midwife]] [[be of good courage|be of good courage, take courage, be over-bold and audacious, have confidence in, venture]], and for [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] to you is son.

greek: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ἀφιέναι αὐτὴν τὴν ψυχήν — ἀπέθνῃσκεν γάρ — ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Υἱὸς ὀδύνης μου· ὁ δὲ πατὴρ ἐκάλεσεν αὐτὸν Βενιαμιν.
hint: And it happened, as she was giving up her soul — for she was dying — she called his name Son of my pain; but the father called him Benjamin.

notes.text: Rahlfs capitalises Υἱὸς: the phrase is the name, the Greek of Hebrew Ben-ʾÔnî.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus adds αὐτοῦ, *his*, marked in the Hexaplaric text with an asterisk.

reading: [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[in|within, inside of, and by means of]] the [[to send forth|to send forth, to discharge, to let go and loose and set free, to let alone and leave, to give up and hand over, to permit and allow]] her [[the breath|the breath, the life, the spirit, life and death, the ghost, the departed soul]] — [[was dying off|was dying off, was dying, was being put to death, was being slain]] for — [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression]] of him [[name:Υἱὸς]] [[of pain of body|of pain of body, of pain of mind, of grief and distress]] of me; the [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], father [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited]] him [[name:Βενιαμιν]].

names.gloss: (Υἱὸς ὀδύνης μου, "son of my pain", the Greek of Hebrew Ben-ʾÔnî)
(Βενιαμιν, from Hebrew Binyāmîn, "son of the right hand" or "son of the south")

greek: ἀπέθανεν δὲ Ραχηλ καὶ ἐτάφη ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ Εφραθα (αὕτη ἐστὶν Βηθλεεμ).
hint: And Rachel died and was buried in the way of Ephrath (this is Bethlehem).

notes.text: θάπτω, *to bury*, and in Middle Liddell also *to honour with funeral rites*: the word covers the rite as well as the act.

reading: [[died off|died off, died, was put to death, was slain]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Ραχηλ]] and [[was buried|was buried, was honoured with funeral rites]] [[in the way|within, inside of, and by means of the way, the path, the track, the road, the highway, the course, the journey, the manner and method]] of [[name:Εφραθα]] ([[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] is [[name:Βηθλεεμ]]).

names.gloss: (Βηθλεεμ, from Hebrew Bêt-Leḥem, "house of bread")

greek: καὶ ἔστησεν Ιακωβ στήλην ἐπὶ τοῦ μνημείου αὐτῆς· αὕτη ἐστὶν στήλη μνημείου Ραχηλ ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.
hint: And Jacob set up a pillar on her tomb; this is the pillar of Rachel's tomb to this day.

notes.text: μνημεῖον, *a memorial*, as at 23:6: the thing that keeps the memory, before it is a grave.

reading: and [[made to stand|made to stand, set, stopped and stayed and checked, set up and raised, established and instituted, appointed, weighed]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[a block of stone|a block of stone, a prop and buttress to a wall, a slab, a gravestone, the record and a contract and agreement, the turning-post]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[of the memorial|of the memorial, of the remembrance, of the record, of the tomb and monument]] of her; [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] is [[a block of stone|a block of stone, a prop and buttress to a wall, a slab, a gravestone, the record and a contract and agreement, the turning-post]] [[of memorial|of memorial, of remembrance, of record, of tomb and monument]] of [[name:Ραχηλ]] [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] the to-day [[of day|of day, of day-break, of time]].

greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἡνίκα κατῴκησεν Ισραηλ ἐν τῇ γῇ ἐκείνῃ, ἐπορεύθη Ρουβην καὶ ἐκοιμήθη μετὰ Βαλλας τῆς παλλακῆς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἤκουσεν Ισραηλ, καὶ πονηρὸν ἐφάνη ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ. Ἦσαν δὲ οἱ υἱοὶ Ιακωβ δώδεκα.
hint: And it happened, when Israel dwelt in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine; and Israel heard, and it appeared evil before him. And the sons of Jacob were twelve.

notes.text: The neuter as a noun with φαίνω: a toilsome thing appeared, where the Hebrew says simply that Israel heard.

notes.lemma: Ἦσαν δὲ οἱ υἱοὶ Ιακωβ δώδεκα
notes.text: The sentence stands in the same verse as Reuben's act, with nothing between them: the twelve are counted where the offence is told.

reading: [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[at which time|at which time, when, since, whenever]] [[dwelt in|dwelt in, settled in, colonised, inhabited, settled and dwelt, lay and was situate]] [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[in the earth|within, inside of, and by means of the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] [[that|that, in order that]], [[was driven|was driven, was carried, went, walked, marched, went across and passed]] [[name:Ρουβην]] and [[fell asleep|fell asleep, went abed and lay abed, slept, fell asleep and died, kept watch at night]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] of [[name:Βαλλας]] [[of the concubine|of the concubine, of the mistress]] of the father of him; and [[heard|heard, had hearing of, heard tell of, hearkened and gave ear, listened to and obeyed]] [[name:Ισραηλ]], and [[toilsome|toilsome, painful, grievous, good-for-nothing, bad and worthless, wicked]] [[was brought to light|was brought to light and made to appear, was shown forth and made known and revealed and disclosed and shown, was made clear and explained and expounded, was informed against and indicted and impeached, was proclaimed, came to light and was seen and appeared, shone brightly, came into being, appeared to be, was manifest]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against]] of him. were, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, the sons of [[name:Ιακωβ]] twelve.

names.gloss: (Ρουβην, from Hebrew Rĕʾûbēn, which the Hebrew of 29:32 hears in rāʾâ bĕʿonyî, "he has seen my affliction")
(Βαλλα, from Hebrew Bilhâ, usually connected with bāhal, "to be troubled")

greek: υἱοὶ Λειας· πρωτότοκος Ιακωβ Ρουβην, Συμεων, Λευι, Ιουδας, Ισσαχαρ, Ζαβουλων.
hint: Sons of Leah: Jacob's firstborn Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun.

notes.text: πρωτότοκος, *firstborn*, the word that carries the whole of Genesis's quarrel over birthright.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Λευεις.

reading: sons of [[name:Λειας]]; [[firstborn|firstborn, first-fruits]] of [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[name:Ρουβην]], [[name:Συμεων]], [[name:Λευι]], [[name:Ιουδας]], [[name:Ισσαχαρ]], [[name:Ζαβουλων]].

names.gloss: (Λεια, from Hebrew Lēʾâ, of uncertain meaning, perhaps "wild cow")
(Συμεων, from Hebrew Šimʿôn, which the Hebrew of 29:33 hears in šāmaʿ, "he heard")
(Λευι, from Hebrew Lēwî, which the Hebrew of 29:34 hears in lāwâ, "he was joined")
(Ιουδας, from Hebrew Yĕhûdâ, which the Hebrew of 29:35 hears in yādâ, "to praise")
(Ισσαχαρ, from Hebrew Yiśśāśkār, which the Hebrew of 30:18 hears in śākār, "wages")
(Ζαβουλων, from Hebrew Zĕbûlûn, which the Hebrew of 30:20 hears in zābal, "to dwell with honour")

greek: υἱοὶ δὲ Ραχηλ· Ιωσηφ καὶ Βενιαμιν.
hint: And sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.

notes.text: The list runs without a verb throughout 35:23-26: the Greek keeps the Hebrew's bare naming.

reading: sons [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], of [[name:Ραχηλ]]; [[name:Ιωσηφ]] and [[name:Βενιαμιν]].

names.gloss: (Ιωσηφ, from Hebrew Yôsēp̄, which the Hebrew of 30:24 hears in yōsēp̄, "may he add")

greek: υἱοὶ δὲ Βαλλας παιδίσκης Ραχηλ· Δαν καὶ Νεφθαλι.
hint: And sons of Bilhah, Rachel's slave-girl: Dan and Naphtali.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Νεφθαλειμ.

reading: sons [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], of [[name:Βαλλας]] [[of a young girl|of a young girl, of a maiden, of a young slave, of a courtesan]] of [[name:Ραχηλ]]; [[name:Δαν]] and [[name:Νεφθαλι]].

names.gloss: (Δαν, from Hebrew Dān, which the Hebrew of 30:6 hears in dîn, "he judged")
(Νεφθαλι, from Hebrew Naptālî, which the Hebrew of 30:8 hears in niptal, "I have wrestled")

greek: υἱοὶ δὲ Ζελφας παιδίσκης Λειας· Γαδ καὶ Ασηρ. οὗτοι υἱοὶ Ιακωβ, οἳ ἐγένοντο αὐτῷ ἐν Μεσοποταμίᾳ τῆς Συρίας.
hint: And sons of Zilpah, Leah's slave-girl: Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Mesopotamia of Syria.

notes.text: [[flag]] All twelve are said to have been born in Mesopotamia, though Benjamin was born at Ephrath in 35:16-18; the Hebrew says the same.

reading: sons [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], of [[name:Ζελφας]] [[of a young girl|of a young girl, of a maiden, of a young slave, of a courtesan]] of [[name:Λειας]]; [[name:Γαδ]] and [[name:Ασηρ]]. [[these|these, the nearer, what follows]] sons of [[name:Ιακωβ]], which [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] to him [[in|within, inside of, and by means of]] [[name:Μεσοποταμίᾳ]] the [[name:Συρίας]].

names.gloss: (Ζελφα, from Hebrew Zilpâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Γαδ, from Hebrew Gād, which the Hebrew of 30:11 hears in gād, "fortune")
(Ασηρ, from Hebrew ʾĀšēr, which the Hebrew of 30:13 hears in ʾōšer, "happiness")

greek: Ἦλθεν δὲ Ιακωβ πρὸς Ισαακ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ εἰς Μαμβρη εἰς πόλιν τοῦ πεδίου (αὕτη ἐστὶν Χεβρων) ἐν γῇ Χανααν, οὗ παρῴκησεν Αβρααμ καὶ Ισαακ.
hint: And Jacob came to Isaac his father at Mamre, to a city of the plain (this is Hebron) in the land of Canaan, where Abraham and Isaac had sojourned.

notes.text: παροικέω, *to dwell beside*, of a resident alien: neither man ever owned the land he lived in.

reading: [[came|came, went, went back and returned, was going to and intended, came within a little of and was near]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] [[name:Ισαακ]] the father of him [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[name:Μαμβρη]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[city|city, citadel, country, body of citizens, state]] [[of the plain|of the plain, of the flat, of the plain flat open country]] ([[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] is [[name:Χεβρων]]) [[in|within, inside of, and by means of]] [[earth|earth, land, the ground]] [[name:Χανααν]], [[where|where, at what point, how, by what right]] [[dwelt beside|dwelt beside, dwelt along the coast of, lived near, dwelt among, lay near, lived in and sojourned]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] and [[name:Ισαακ]].

names.gloss: (Μαμβρη, from Hebrew Mamrēʾ, of uncertain meaning)
(Χεβρων, from Hebrew Ḥebrôn, usually connected with ḥābar, "to join")

greek: ἐγένοντο δὲ αἱ ἡμέραι Ισαακ, ἃς ἔζησεν, ἔτη ἑκατὸν ὀγδοήκοντα·
hint: And the days of Isaac which he lived were a hundred and eighty years;

notes.text: ζάω, *to live*, with the days as its object: the Greek counts the days he lived, not the years he was.

reading: [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], the days of [[name:Ισαακ]], which [[lived|lived, was in full life and strength, was fresh and strong]], years hundred eighty;

greek: καὶ ἐκλιπὼν ἀπέθανεν καὶ προσετέθη πρὸς τὸ γένος αὐτοῦ πρεσβύτερος καὶ πλήρης ἡμερῶν, καὶ ἔθαψαν αὐτὸν Ησαυ καὶ Ιακωβ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ.
hint: and failing he died and was gathered to his race, an old man and full of days, and Esau and Jacob his sons buried him.

notes.text: ἐκλείπω, *to leave out*, and so *to fail, die away*: the Greek says he left off before it says he died.
προστίθημι in the passive, *was put to*: the dead man is added to his kin, as at 25:8 and 25:17.

reading: and [[having left out|having left out, having omitted and passed over, having forsaken and deserted and abandoned, having suffered an eclipse, having died, having left off and ceased and stopped, having failed and been wanting]] [[died off|died off, died, was put to death, was slain]] and [[was put to|was put to, was handed over and delivered, was given and bestowed, was imposed further, was attributed, was added]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] [[the race|the race, the stock and family, the offspring and posterity, the clan and house, the tribe and caste, the breed, the age and generation, the sex and gender, the class and sort]] of him [[elder|elder, older, higher and more important, greater than, elders of the Jewish Council, elders of the Church and presbyters]] and [[full|full, filled, complete, satisfied, whole and entire]] [[of days|of days, of day-breaks, of times]], and [[buried|buried, honoured with funeral rites]] him [[name:Ησαυ]] and [[name:Ιακωβ]] the sons of him.
